questiontext.text: Why did the Allies adopt the Europe First strategy?

answer.text: They viewed Nazi Germany as the most immediate strategic threat while still resisting Japan.
They had already defeated Germany before Pearl Harbor.
They planned to abandon the Pacific permanently.
They believed Japan was allied with Britain.

questiontext.text: What made the Battle of Midway a major turning point?

answer.text: American forces destroyed key Japanese carriers and shifted the strategic initiative.
It opened the Normandy beachhead.
It caused Germany's surrender.
It was fought entirely in North Africa.

questiontext.text: What was the strategic purpose of D-Day?

answer.text: To establish an Allied foothold in Western Europe and open a major front against Germany
To capture Tokyo
To defend Pearl Harbor from its first attack
To end the Battle of the Atlantic in 1941

questiontext.text: How did island hopping support the Allied advance?

answer.text: It secured useful bases and moved forces toward Japan while bypassing some strongholds.
It required capturing every Japanese-held island.
It shifted all forces away from the Pacific.
It was a diplomatic agreement with the Soviet Union.

questiontext.text: Which evidence best supports the claim that World War II required global strategy?

answer.text: Allied leaders coordinated campaigns, shipping, resources, and priorities across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Pacific.
Every battle occurred in one country.
Civilian production was unrelated to military operations.
The Allies fought without coordinating objectives.
